stem: A routine crop walk begins at the room entrance where one plant is visibly abnormal. What is the strongest next step before describing the room-level condition?
choices: Follow the supplied representative route and compare multiple locations before describing the room-level pattern
Inspect the rest of the doorway row first and use that row to represent the room if no second abnormal plant appears
Document the plant and its two nearest neighbors, then make a room-level statement from that local comparison
Focus the walk on plants that appear different so the technician captures the most important abnormalities efficiently
rationale: A conspicuous entry-point plant and a small local comparison do not establish room-level distribution. The planned representative route preserves broader sampling context before a room-level statement is made.

extensions.sourceScope: Transferable greenhouse scouting and recordkeeping guidance; not a universal cannabis sampling prescription.
